name: Lava glazing
summary: A thick glaze that blisters and runs in the kiln. It leaves a rough, cratered surface like cooled lava, often in two or more colours.
how: Mix a glaze with a high content of frit and a gas-forming additive.
Apply it in a layer 2 to 4 mm thick over a base glaze.
Fire it so that the layer blisters and runs.
Cool the kiln slowly so that the crater surface sets.

origin.note: Factories in the Westerwald region start to sell vases with a thick, bubbling volcanic glaze.

adoptions.via: West German factories fire heavy vases in thick, cratered glazes of orange, brown and black.
